tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Theo ( @t3dotgg ) found the real tradeoff. Sonnet 5 doesn't always know when to tap out. On hard tasks it grinds and keeps spawning sub-agents instead of escalating, and it burned close to 2x Opus's tokens in his testing. Cheap per token doesn't guarantee cheap per task.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Pricing is where it gets interesting. $2 input / $10 output per million tokens through August 31, jumping to $3/$15 after. Opus runs $15/$75. On paper that's a massive gap. One catch: the new tokenizer burns 1 to 1.35x more tokens than Sonnet 4.6 for the same input, so the savings aren't quite as clean as the sticker price.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The numbers back it up. 63.2% on SWE-bench Pro, up from 57.6% on Sonnet 4.6, and it actually edges out Opus 4.8 on GDPval-AA v2, the benchmark that looks the most like real sustained agent work. One tester watched it write a failing test, fix the bug, then rerun the test to confirm, all unprompted in a single pass.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Claude Sonnet 5 just dropped, and it's doing something no other model does out of the box: spinning up its own sub-agents without being asked. It's live in Kilo Code right now.
